attributes.title: Preregistration: Block I B1 Gray-Scott Driven-Pattern Baseline - Theory of Everything Research Programme.
attributes.description:
This preregistration freezes the confirmatory design for the B1 Gray-Scott driven-pattern baseline in Experimental Block I of the Theory of Everything Research Programme. The study tests the deliberately limited claim that sustained non-equilibrium driving can support reproducible non-trivial spatial organisation in a Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion system. It does not test or establish self-maintenance, organisational closure, biological life, intelligence, consciousness, or resolution of Transition Problem 1.

Five confirmatory conditions are preregistered: a sustained pattern-forming regime, a matched non-pattern comparator, removal of driving, standardised local damage, and a periodic-to-no-flux boundary modification. Ten explicit held-out confirmatory seeds, primary estimands, intervention timings, decision thresholds, invalid-run criteria and provenance requirements were frozen before confirmatory execution. Three development-only pilot seeds were used before preregistration to validate the implementation and refine measurement definitions; those pilot outcomes are disclosed and excluded from confirmatory evidence.

The confirmatory execution gate remains closed at registration. The experiment will be unlocked only after the public OSF registration has been created. Related experimental programme: Craggs, K. (2026), Testing a Candidate Dependency Architecture: An Adversarial Experimental Programme for Maintenance, Heredity, Learning, Agency and Self-Modelling, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22857230.
tags: Theory of Everything; preregistration; simulation study; Gray-Scott; reaction-diffusion; non-equilibrium dynamics; pattern formation; adversarial experimentation; reproducibility; open science

344-2.value:
The study evaluates whether sustained non-equilibrium driving can support reproducible non-trivial spatial organisation in a Gray–Scott reaction–diffusion system, while explicitly distinguishing persistent driven pattern formation from self-maintenance.

The preregistered hypotheses are:

H_B1_BASE_01_PATTERN — Sustained pattern regime. Under the frozen pattern-forming parameters and sustained driving, the Gray–Scott system will exhibit reproducible non-trivial spatial heterogeneity at the registered terminal horizon.
H_B1_BASE_02_NONPATTERN — Non-pattern comparator. Under the frozen comparator parameters and sustained driving, the system will approach an effectively spatially homogeneous V field at the registered terminal horizon.
H_B1_BASE_03_DRIVE_DEPENDENCE — Dependence on sustained driving. After a pattern has formed, registered removal of the feed/driving term at PDE step 3500 will cause spatial heterogeneity to collapse within the preregistered observation window.
H_B1_BASE_04_DAMAGE_RECOVERY — Local damage and recovery. With sustained driving retained, a registered local perturbation at PDE step 3500 will produce a large selective deficit in the damaged central region followed by recovery towards the preregistered pre-damage level.
H_B1_BASE_05_BOUNDARY_ROBUSTNESS — Boundary robustness. A pattern established with periodic boundaries will remain quantitatively non-trivial after a registered change to no-flux boundaries at PDE step 3500.

The overall B1 question is whether a sustained-driving pattern regime can be quantitatively distinguished from a matched non-pattern regime, shown to depend reproducibly upon continued external driving, and characterised under registered perturbation and boundary modification.

A positive result will establish only that driven Gray–Scott dynamics can sustain reproducible spatial organisation under the tested conditions. It will not be interpreted as evidence of self-maintenance, organisational closure, biological life, intelligence, consciousness, or resolution of Transition Problem 1.

344-4.value: Data does not yet exist. No part of the data that will be used for this analysis plan exists, and no part will be generated until after this plan is registered.

344-14.value:
No confirmatory data for this preregistered analysis currently exists. None of the ten registered confirmatory seeds has been executed, inspected or analysed, and confirmatory execution is software-gated until this preregistration has been made public.

Before freezing the confirmatory protocol, three development-only pilot seeds were run across the five B1 conditions. These pilot data are not part of the confirmatory dataset and will not be used as confirmatory evidence. The pilot was used to validate the implementation, identify defective measurements and finalise a pilot-informed confirmatory protocol.

Pilot inspection showed that normalised mutual-information and spectral measures could appear spuriously large when field amplitude was effectively zero. An amplitude gate of \(10^{-5}\) in V-field standard deviation was therefore introduced for those descriptive measures. A central-region probe was also added so that the local-damage intervention would be measured in the region actually perturbed rather than diluted over the full lattice.

The confirmatory thresholds, measurement definitions and version 1.1.0 manifests are therefore explicitly pilot-informed. To reduce unintended influence from the pilot, the ten confirmatory seeds were generated separately and are disjoint from the three development seeds; the confirmatory hypotheses, primary estimands, intervention timings, thresholds and decision rules were frozen before registration; all five confirmatory manifests have fixed SHA-256 hashes; and the execution gate remains closed until public preregistration.

Any later unplanned analyses will be labelled exploratory and will not replace a failed preregistered primary criterion.

value: Simulation study: Using existing or synthetic data to assess performance of a model, mimic operation of an existing or proposed system, or predict possible outcomes in a controlled context. This may include demonstration of methods, many varieties of modeling, prediction of policy impacts, simulating behavior or outcomes in a population, and other designs.

Direct inference on causal relationship(s): This study is intended to infer or estimate a causal relationship between two or more variables. It is designed specifically for the purposes of causal inference or identification.

344-38.value:
No conventional blinding is used because the study consists entirely of computational simulations with preregistered conditions and automated quantitative analysis. Instead, unintended researcher influence is reduced through procedural controls.

The five confirmatory conditions, ten confirmatory seeds, environment versions, intervention timings, primary estimands, thresholds and decision rules are frozen before confirmatory execution. The ten confirmatory seeds have not been executed or inspected at the time of registration and are disjoint from the development-pilot seeds. Confirmatory execution is software-gated until public preregistration.

Primary analyses, figures, tables and decision records are generated automatically from archived raw trajectories rather than through manual coding or visual classification. Pattern-forming outcomes are evaluated using preregistered quantitative criteria rather than researcher selection of visually interesting results. Any analyses introduced after inspection of confirmatory outcomes will be labelled exploratory and will not replace failed preregistered criteria.

344-44.value:
No random assignment of subjects or experimental units to conditions is used. This is a computational simulation study with five conditions specified prospectively in frozen manifests.

Ten explicit confirmatory seeds are preregistered before execution. Where conditions share the same initialisation structure, the same seed set is used across conditions to support paired comparison and reduce variation attributable to initialisation. Seeds are not selected, replaced or excluded on the basis of observed confirmatory outcomes.

The confirmatory seed set is disjoint from the three development-pilot seeds and had not been executed at the time of preregistration.

344-53.value:
The sample size of ten confirmatory seeds per condition was fixed prospectively after development-pilot validation and before any confirmatory seed was executed.

B1 is designed as a small, interpretable baseline experiment intended to establish whether large, preregistered differences between pattern-forming and non-pattern-forming regimes, and between intact and experimentally manipulated driven systems, are reproducible across independent initialisations. The study is not designed to estimate a small population effect or to infer a biological population parameter.

No post hoc power calculation using confirmatory outcomes will determine sample size. The ten-seed design was selected as a fixed replication requirement that balances computational tractability with protection against conclusions based on a single initial condition or a very small number of simulations.

The confirmatory decision rules are based on the preregistered quantitative thresholds and the consistency of the effect across the fixed seed set. The sample size will not be increased because an observed result is borderline or unfavourable. Additional replications, if later undertaken, will be reported as a new replication study rather than incorporated retrospectively into this preregistered confirmatory sample.

344-55.value:
Development and confirmatory data collection are strictly separated.

Pilot testing ended after three development-only seeds had been used to verify the Gray–Scott implementation, inspect the behaviour of the five planned conditions, identify defective measurement procedures and finalise the version 1.1.0 confirmatory protocol. Those pilot data are excluded from the confirmatory dataset.

Confirmatory data collection begins only after:

this preregistration has been made public;
the five version 1.1.0 confirmatory manifests and associated lock files remain unchanged and pass integrity verification;
the ten registered confirmatory seeds remain unexecuted;
the confirmatory software execution gate is formally changed to CLEARED_FOR_CONFIRMATORY_EXECUTION.

Data collection will terminate after all five preregistered conditions have been executed for all ten confirmatory seeds, yielding 50 valid condition-level runs, unless a preregistered invalid-run condition prevents completion of a particular run.

There is no sequential stopping rule based on observed scientific outcomes. Data collection will not stop early because a hypothesis appears strongly supported, clearly rejected or unlikely to change with further runs.

If a run is technically invalid because of a preregistered execution or provenance failure, that run will be marked INVALID_RUN, preserved in the audit record and rerun using the same registered seed after the technical problem has been corrected. Such replacement does not alter the planned confirmatory sample.

No new seeds or additional confirmatory runs will be added in response to the observed B1 results. Any extension beyond the fixed ten-seed confirmatory design will require a separately identified replication or follow-up study.

344-58.value:
None.

This study does not use random assignment of subjects or experimental units to treatments. It is a preregistered computational simulation study with five deterministic conditions specified in frozen manifests.

The simulation conditions differ prospectively in Gray–Scott parameter regime and registered interventions, including sustained versus removed driving, local damage, and periodic versus no-flux boundary conditions. These condition differences are described in the Study Design section and the attached preregistration record, but they are not classified here as randomized manipulated variables because no randomization to treatment arms is used.

344-62.value:
The primary recorded data are the two Gray–Scott concentration fields, \(U\) and \(V\), on a \(64 \times 64\) spatial grid. Raw \(U\) and \(V\) field states are archived at every registered observation, occurring every 20 PDE steps from initialization through PDE step 6000.

The following variables are recorded or computed from each registered simulation state:

1. **PDE step:** the current numerical time step.

2. **Mean \(U\) concentration (`u_mean`):** the arithmetic mean of all \(U\)-field lattice values.

3. **Mean \(V\) concentration (`v_mean`):** the arithmetic mean of all \(V\)-field lattice values.

4. **Whole-field \(V\) standard deviation (`v_std`):** the spatial standard deviation of the \(V\) field across all \(64 \times 64\) lattice sites. This is the principal quantitative measure of spatial heterogeneity used in the sustained-pattern, non-pattern, drive-removal and boundary-modification conditions.

5. **Maximum \(V\) concentration (`v_max`):** the maximum \(V\)-field value in the lattice.

6. **Central-region mean \(V\) (`center_v_mean`):** the mean \(V\) concentration within the registered central square occupying 25 percent of the linear grid extent. This variable is used for the local-damage and recovery analysis.

7. **Central-region \(V\) standard deviation (`center_v_std`):** the spatial standard deviation of \(V\) within the same registered central region.

8. **Active spatial fraction (`active_fraction_v_gt_0_05`):** the fraction of lattice sites for which \(V > 0.05\).

9. **Adjacent-cell spatial mutual information (`spatial_mutual_information`):** a descriptive measure of dependence between neighbouring \(V\)-field concentrations, calculated after discretising the \(V\) field into 12 bins and averaging horizontal and vertical adjacent-cell mutual information. The value is set to zero when whole-field \(V\) standard deviation is below the preregistered amplitude floor of \(10^{-5}\).

10. **Spectral peak fraction (`spectral_peak_fraction`):** a descriptive Fourier-domain measure calculated from the mean-centred \(V\) field as the largest non-DC Fourier power divided by total non-DC Fourier power. The value is set to zero when \(V\)-field standard deviation is below the preregistered amplitude floor of \(10^{-5}\).

11. **Feed/driving status:** whether the registered Gray–Scott feed term remains active at the current observation.

12. **Boundary condition:** the active boundary condition, recorded as periodic or no-flux for the preregistered B1 conditions.

13. **Registered intervention status:** which, if any, preregistered intervention has occurred, including drive removal, local damage or boundary modification.

14. **Seed identity:** the explicit preregistered confirmatory simulation seed associated with the run.

The confirmatory analysis additionally derives condition-specific outcome variables from these measurements: terminal \(V\)-field standard deviation, time to heterogeneity collapse after drive removal, immediate central-region damage fraction, time to 90-percent central-region recovery, terminal recovery fraction, and terminal heterogeneity after boundary modification.

Variables used to identify technically invalid runs are also recorded through the provenance system, including manifest and configuration hashes, seed consistency, software/source version, numerical-finiteness checks and raw-data integrity checks. These variables are used only to determine execution validity and are not scientific exclusion criteria based on the observed hypothesis outcome.

344-66.value:
No composite scalar measure of organisation, viability or self-maintenance will be constructed. The registered quantities remain separate because they answer different descriptive or intervention-specific questions.

The principal derived variables are defined as follows.

**1. Whole-field spatial heterogeneity**

For a \(V\) field containing \(N\) lattice sites,

$$
s_V =
\sqrt{
\frac{1}{N}
\sum_{i=1}^{N}
(V_i-\bar V)^2
}.
$$

The terminal heterogeneity measure is \(s_V\) at PDE step 6000.

For the sustained-pattern condition, the primary group-level estimand is the arithmetic mean of terminal \(s_V\) across the ten preregistered seeds.

For the non-pattern comparator, the same terminal quantity is used, allowing the two regimes to be assessed using the same measurement definition.

**2. Time to collapse after drive removal**

Driving is removed at PDE step 3500. For each seed, collapse time is

$$
T_{\mathrm{collapse}}
=
\min \{t-3500 : s_V(t) \leq 0.005\}.
$$

If the threshold is not reached during the registered post-intervention observation window, the run is recorded as not meeting the registered collapse criterion.

The secondary drive-removal measure is terminal \(s_V\) at PDE step 6000.

**3. Immediate local-damage fraction**

Let \(C_{\mathrm{pre}}\) denote the central-region mean \(V\) value at the last registered observation before the local-damage intervention, and let \(C_{\mathrm{post}}\) denote the corresponding value immediately after the registered perturbation.

The immediate retained fraction is

$$
R_{\mathrm{immediate}}
=
\frac{C_{\mathrm{post}}}{C_{\mathrm{pre}}}.
$$

The proportional deficit is

$$
D_{\mathrm{immediate}}
=
1-R_{\mathrm{immediate}}.
$$

A reduction of at least 50 percent corresponds to \(R_{\mathrm{immediate}} \leq 0.5\).

**4. Local-damage recovery time**

Recovery time is the first registered post-damage time at which central-region mean \(V\) returns to at least 90 percent of its pre-damage value:

$$
T_{\mathrm{recovery}}
=
\min\{t-3500 :
C(t) \geq 0.9\,C_{\mathrm{pre}}\}.
$$

The terminal recovery fraction is

$$
R_{\mathrm{terminal}}
=
\frac{C(6000)}{C_{\mathrm{pre}}}.
$$

**5. Boundary-robustness measure**

For the boundary-modification condition, the principal derived measure is terminal whole-field \(V\) standard deviation at PDE step 6000 after the boundary is changed from periodic to no-flux at PDE step 3500.

**6. Adjacent-cell spatial mutual information**

The \(V\) field is discretised into 12 equally spaced bins spanning its observed minimum-to-maximum range. Mutual information for adjacent-cell pairs is calculated as

$$
I(X;Y)
=
\sum_{x,y}
p(x,y)
\log
\frac{p(x,y)}
{p(x)p(y)}.
$$

Horizontal and vertical adjacent-cell mutual information values are averaged. Under periodic boundaries, neighbouring cells wrap across the lattice edges; under non-periodic boundaries only existing adjacent pairs are included.

If whole-field \(s_V < 10^{-5}\), spatial mutual information is set to zero. This preregistered amplitude gate prevents numerical remnants of an effectively homogeneous field from being interpreted as meaningful spatial structure.

**7. Spectral peak fraction**

The \(V\) field is first mean-centred. A two-dimensional discrete Fourier transform is calculated and squared magnitudes provide Fourier power. The zero-frequency/DC component is removed.

The spectral peak fraction is

$$
S_{\mathrm{peak}}
=
\frac{
\max_{\mathbf{k}\neq 0} P(\mathbf{k})
}{
\sum_{\mathbf{k}\neq 0}P(\mathbf{k})
}.
$$

If whole-field \(s_V < 10^{-5}\), this descriptor is set to zero.

Spatial mutual information and spectral peak fraction are secondary descriptive pattern measures only. They are not interpreted as measures of self-maintenance, viability or a universal degree of organisation.

**8. Condition-level seed counts**

Several preregistered decision rules additionally use the number of seeds satisfying a fixed quantitative criterion, for example the number of seeds with terminal \(s_V \geq 0.04\), the number reaching \(s_V \leq 0.005\) within 500 PDE steps after drive removal, or the number recovering to at least 90 percent of the pre-damage central-region mean within 500 PDE steps.

These counts are used only according to the preregistered condition-specific decision rules. They are not combined into a general hierarchy or organisation index.

344-71.value:
The primary confirmatory analysis does not use ANOVA, regression, structural equation modelling or another fitted parametric model. The preregistered hypotheses are evaluated using fixed quantitative estimands and decision thresholds specified before confirmatory execution.

All analyses are performed first at the individual-seed level and then aggregated across the ten preregistered confirmatory seeds. The same seed identities are used across conditions where the initialisation structure is shared, allowing paired descriptive comparisons, but the primary decisions are determined by the preregistered condition-specific rules rather than by null-hypothesis significance tests.

The five primary analyses are:

C1: Sustained pattern regime.
The primary estimand is the mean terminal (V)-field standard deviation at PDE step 6000 across the ten registered seeds. The analysis also counts how many seeds have terminal (V)-field standard deviation of at least 0.04.

C2: Non-pattern comparator.
The primary estimand is the mean terminal (V)-field standard deviation at PDE step 6000. The analysis also counts how many seeds have terminal (V)-field standard deviation at or below 0.005.

C3: Dependence on sustained driving.
For each seed, the primary estimand is the number of PDE steps elapsed after removal of driving at step 3500 until whole-field (V)-field standard deviation first reaches or falls below 0.005. The analysis counts the number of seeds meeting this collapse threshold within 500 PDE steps. Mean terminal (V)-field standard deviation at PDE step 6000 is a secondary registered estimand.

C4: Local damage and recovery.
For each seed, the immediate proportional reduction in central-region mean (V) following local damage is calculated relative to the last registered pre-damage value. Recovery time is the number of PDE steps after damage until central-region mean (V) first reaches at least 90 percent of its pre-damage value. The analysis counts the number of seeds showing an immediate reduction of at least 50 percent and subsequent recovery within 500 PDE steps.

C5: Boundary robustness.
The primary estimand is terminal whole-field (V)-field standard deviation at PDE step 6000 after the registered change from periodic to no-flux boundaries at step 3500. The analysis counts the number of seeds with terminal standard deviation of at least 0.04.

The sustained non-pattern comparator functions as a negative control for persistent spatial heterogeneity. The sustained pattern condition functions as the reference condition for the intervention analyses. Drive removal, local damage and boundary modification are registered interventions whose effects are evaluated against the corresponding frozen pre-intervention trajectory and/or sustained-driving reference.

No statistical model will be substituted if a preregistered threshold is not met. Any additional fitted model or inferential test introduced after confirmatory outcomes are observed will be labelled exploratory and will not replace the registered primary decision rules.

344-77.value:
Primary inference is based on preregistered quantitative decision rules rather than (p)-values, confidence-level significance thresholds, Bayes factors or model-fit indices. No one-tailed or two-tailed null-hypothesis significance tests are used for the primary decisions.

The condition-specific criteria are:

C1: Sustained pattern regime

Retain: mean terminal (V)-field standard deviation (\geq 0.05), and at least 9 of 10 seeds have terminal standard deviation (\geq 0.04).
Restrict: mean terminal standard deviation (\geq 0.02), but the Retain criterion is not met.
Reject: mean terminal standard deviation (<0.02), or the regime cannot be distinguished reproducibly from the matched non-pattern comparator.

C2: Non-pattern comparator

Retain: mean terminal (V)-field standard deviation (\leq 0.005), and at least 9 of 10 seeds are (\leq 0.005).
Restrict: mean terminal standard deviation (>0.005) but (\leq0.02).
Reject: mean terminal standard deviation (>0.02).

C3: Dependence on sustained driving

Retain: at least 9 of 10 seeds reach (V)-field standard deviation (\leq0.005) within 500 PDE steps after drive removal, and mean terminal standard deviation is (\leq0.005).
Restrict: quantitative collapse occurs in at least 8 of 10 seeds but exceeds the 500-step window or leaves terminal residual structure above 0.005.
Reduce: equivalent persistent patterning continues after drive removal, reducing the explanatory role assigned to sustained driving for this regime.
Reject: fewer than 8 of 10 seeds show quantitative collapse after registered drive removal.

C4: Local damage and recovery

Retain: at least 8 of 10 seeds show an immediate central-region mean-(V) reduction of at least 50 percent and recover to at least 90 percent of the pre-damage value within 500 PDE steps.
Restrict: damage is quantitatively effective but recovery occurs in fewer than 8 of 10 seeds or requires more than 500 PDE steps.
Reject: the registered perturbation fails to produce a selective local deficit or no reproducible recovery occurs under sustained driving.

C5: Boundary robustness

Retain: at least 8 of 10 seeds have terminal (V)-field standard deviation (\geq0.04).
Restrict: non-trivial heterogeneity remains but fewer than 8 of 10 seeds meet the 0.04 threshold.
Reject: the registered boundary modification eliminates reproducible non-trivial spatial heterogeneity.

The overall B1 verdict is assigned only after all five registered conditions have valid provenance and analysis records:

Retain: C1, C2 and C3 each meet their Retain criteria. C4 and C5 are reported as robustness characterisation.
Restrict: the core pattern/non-pattern/drive-dependence result is otherwise retained but one or both robustness tests show material sensitivity, or one core condition reaches only its Restrict criterion.
Reduce: the matched comparator or drive-removal condition reproduces the decisive persistence result such that the nominated pattern regime or sustained driving adds no selective explanatory value.
Suspend: a decisive condition is invalid, provenance-incomplete, numerically unstable or otherwise uninterpretable under the frozen protocol.
Reject: the sustained pattern regime is not quantitatively distinguishable from the comparator or reproducible dependence upon sustained driving is not demonstrated.

No multiple-testing correction is applied because the five hypotheses are not being searched for significance across a family of interchangeable null-hypothesis tests. Each has a separate preregistered estimand and decision rule, and the overall B1 verdict is itself preregistered. Secondary analyses cannot substitute for a failed primary criterion.

344-81.value:
No statistical imputation of missing confirmatory data is planned.

The protocol is designed to generate a complete set of registered outputs for every valid simulation run. If required raw fields, primary measurements, registered observations or provenance records are missing because of a technical execution failure, that run will not be analysed as partially observed scientific evidence. It will be classified as INVALID_RUN, the failure will be preserved in the audit record, and the same preregistered seed may be rerun after the technical cause has been corrected.

Seeds will not be replaced with new seeds because data are missing or because a run produces an unfavourable scientific outcome.

If a required condition cannot be completed validly after documented technical correction attempts, the missing decisive evidence will not be imputed or ignored. The relevant hypothesis or overall B1 judgement will be eligible for SUSPEND because the preregistered evidence required for interpretation is incomplete.

344-83.value:
Several secondary analyses are preregistered for descriptive and robustness purposes.

Adjacent-cell spatial mutual information and spectral peak fraction will be reported as secondary descriptors of spatial pattern structure. Both are subject to the preregistered (V)-field amplitude gate of (10^{-5}). These measures are not interpreted as scalar measures of organisation, viability or self-maintenance.

Per-seed trajectories of whole-field (V)-field standard deviation will be plotted to show temporal behaviour rather than only terminal aggregates. The local-damage condition will additionally report central-region trajectories so the immediate deficit and recovery process are visible.

Paired descriptive comparisons across conditions may be reported because the same ten seed identities are used where initialisation structures are shared. These comparisons may include per-seed differences in terminal heterogeneity and intervention-response timing. They are secondary to the registered categorical decision rules.

Raw and processed results will also be inspected for numerical stability and consistency with the registered intervention timing. Such checks are quality-control procedures rather than alternative hypothesis tests.

Any additional analysis conceived after the confirmatory results have been observed, including new statistical models, alternative thresholds, alternative spatial descriptors or post hoc subgrouping, will be explicitly labelled exploratory. Exploratory analyses may motivate a future preregistration but will not replace, reinterpret or rescue a failed preregistered primary criterion.

344-86.value:
This preregistration forms the first confirmatory experimental study within the Theory of Everything Research Programme described in the published Programme Overview and Working Papers I--III.

B1 is intentionally narrow. It does not test self-maintenance directly and does not attempt to establish life, autonomy, organisational closure or any higher-order dependency in the programme. Its role is to provide a controlled physical baseline demonstrating whether sustained non-equilibrium driving can support reproducible spatial organisation in a Gray--Scott reaction--diffusion system, and to characterise how that organisation responds to removal of driving, local perturbation and a change of boundary condition.

This distinction is methodologically important because persistent organisation must not be conflated with internally generated maintenance. B1 therefore establishes, at most, the weaker relation:

$$
\text{sustained non-equilibrium driving}
\longrightarrow
\text{persistent organised pattern}.
$$

It does not establish:

$$
\text{persistent organised pattern}
\longrightarrow
\text{self-maintenance}.
$$

A separate subsequent B2 experiment is planned to test causal maintenance architectures more directly through comparisons among passive persistence, external maintenance, internal feed-forward maintenance and reciprocal internal maintenance, including targeted ablation and functional rescue. Results from B1 will not be used to assume the outcome of B2.

Three development-only pilot seeds were used before this preregistration to validate the implementation and measurement procedures. Those pilot runs revealed two measurement issues: normalised spatial-pattern measures could appear spuriously large when field amplitude was effectively zero, and whole-lattice averaging could dilute the effect of a local-damage intervention. The confirmatory protocol was therefore revised before registration to include a \(V\)-field amplitude gate of \(10^{-5}\) for the relevant descriptive pattern measures and a registered central-region measure for the damage-and-recovery condition.

The resulting version 1.1.0 confirmatory protocol is explicitly pilot-informed. The ten confirmatory seeds are separate from the three development seeds and had not been executed, inspected or analysed when this preregistration was prepared. The confirmatory manifests, environment configurations, intervention definitions, seed set, estimands, thresholds and decision rules were frozen before registration and are accompanied by SHA-256 integrity records.

The experiment is implemented within a reproducible infrastructure developed before B1. That infrastructure provides manifest validation, frozen configuration checking, seed registration, raw trajectory logging, provenance capture, automated analysis, figure and table generation, machine-readable decision records and integrity verification. A confirmatory execution gate prevents the registered ten-seed study from running until this preregistration has been made public.

Any departure from the preregistered protocol after confirmatory execution begins will be documented explicitly. Analyses developed after inspection of confirmatory outcomes will be labelled exploratory and will not replace the registered primary decision criteria.

The broader methodological principle is that the experimental programme is designed to remove unsupported structure rather than preserve a preferred hierarchy. A valid negative result, restriction or successful alternative explanation is therefore treated as scientifically informative rather than as a failure of the programme.

registration_responses.344-44:
No random assignment of subjects or experimental units to conditions is used. This is a computational simulation study with five conditions specified prospectively in frozen manifests.

Ten explicit confirmatory seeds are preregistered before execution. Where conditions share the same initialisation structure, the same seed set is used across conditions to support paired comparison and reduce variation attributable to initialisation. Seeds are not selected, replaced or excluded on the basis of observed confirmatory outcomes.

The confirmatory seed set is disjoint from the three development-pilot seeds and had not been executed at the time of preregistration.
registration_responses.344-53:
The sample size of ten confirmatory seeds per condition was fixed prospectively after development-pilot validation and before any confirmatory seed was executed.

B1 is designed as a small, interpretable baseline experiment intended to establish whether large, preregistered differences between pattern-forming and non-pattern-forming regimes, and between intact and experimentally manipulated driven systems, are reproducible across independent initialisations. The study is not designed to estimate a small population effect or to infer a biological population parameter.

No post hoc power calculation using confirmatory outcomes will determine sample size. The ten-seed design was selected as a fixed replication requirement that balances computational tractability with protection against conclusions based on a single initial condition or a very small number of simulations.

The confirmatory decision rules are based on the preregistered quantitative thresholds and the consistency of the effect across the fixed seed set. The sample size will not be increased because an observed result is borderline or unfavourable. Additional replications, if later undertaken, will be reported as a new replication study rather than incorporated retrospectively into this preregistered confirmatory sample.
registration_responses.344-55:
Development and confirmatory data collection are strictly separated.

Pilot testing ended after three development-only seeds had been used to verify the Gray–Scott implementation, inspect the behaviour of the five planned conditions, identify defective measurement procedures and finalise the version 1.1.0 confirmatory protocol. Those pilot data are excluded from the confirmatory dataset.

Confirmatory data collection begins only after:

this preregistration has been made public;
the five version 1.1.0 confirmatory manifests and associated lock files remain unchanged and pass integrity verification;
the ten registered confirmatory seeds remain unexecuted;
the confirmatory software execution gate is formally changed to CLEARED_FOR_CONFIRMATORY_EXECUTION.

Data collection will terminate after all five preregistered conditions have been executed for all ten confirmatory seeds, yielding 50 valid condition-level runs, unless a preregistered invalid-run condition prevents completion of a particular run.

There is no sequential stopping rule based on observed scientific outcomes. Data collection will not stop early because a hypothesis appears strongly supported, clearly rejected or unlikely to change with further runs.

If a run is technically invalid because of a preregistered execution or provenance failure, that run will be marked INVALID_RUN, preserved in the audit record and rerun using the same registered seed after the technical problem has been corrected. Such replacement does not alter the planned confirmatory sample.

No new seeds or additional confirmatory runs will be added in response to the observed B1 results. Any extension beyond the fixed ten-seed confirmatory design will require a separately identified replication or follow-up study.
registration_responses.344-58:
None.

This study does not use random assignment of subjects or experimental units to treatments. It is a preregistered computational simulation study with five deterministic conditions specified in frozen manifests.

The simulation conditions differ prospectively in Gray–Scott parameter regime and registered interventions, including sustained versus removed driving, local damage, and periodic versus no-flux boundary conditions. These condition differences are described in the Study Design section and the attached preregistration record, but they are not classified here as randomized manipulated variables because no randomization to treatment arms is used.
registration_responses.344-62:
The primary recorded data are the two Gray–Scott concentration fields, \(U\) and \(V\), on a \(64 \times 64\) spatial grid. Raw \(U\) and \(V\) field states are archived at every registered observation, occurring every 20 PDE steps from initialization through PDE step 6000.

The following variables are recorded or computed from each registered simulation state:

1. **PDE step:** the current numerical time step.

2. **Mean \(U\) concentration (`u_mean`):** the arithmetic mean of all \(U\)-field lattice values.

3. **Mean \(V\) concentration (`v_mean`):** the arithmetic mean of all \(V\)-field lattice values.

4. **Whole-field \(V\) standard deviation (`v_std`):** the spatial standard deviation of the \(V\) field across all \(64 \times 64\) lattice sites. This is the principal quantitative measure of spatial heterogeneity used in the sustained-pattern, non-pattern, drive-removal and boundary-modification conditions.

5. **Maximum \(V\) concentration (`v_max`):** the maximum \(V\)-field value in the lattice.

6. **Central-region mean \(V\) (`center_v_mean`):** the mean \(V\) concentration within the registered central square occupying 25 percent of the linear grid extent. This variable is used for the local-damage and recovery analysis.

7. **Central-region \(V\) standard deviation (`center_v_std`):** the spatial standard deviation of \(V\) within the same registered central region.

8. **Active spatial fraction (`active_fraction_v_gt_0_05`):** the fraction of lattice sites for which \(V > 0.05\).

9. **Adjacent-cell spatial mutual information (`spatial_mutual_information`):** a descriptive measure of dependence between neighbouring \(V\)-field concentrations, calculated after discretising the \(V\) field into 12 bins and averaging horizontal and vertical adjacent-cell mutual information. The value is set to zero when whole-field \(V\) standard deviation is below the preregistered amplitude floor of \(10^{-5}\).

10. **Spectral peak fraction (`spectral_peak_fraction`):** a descriptive Fourier-domain measure calculated from the mean-centred \(V\) field as the largest non-DC Fourier power divided by total non-DC Fourier power. The value is set to zero when \(V\)-field standard deviation is below the preregistered amplitude floor of \(10^{-5}\).

11. **Feed/driving status:** whether the registered Gray–Scott feed term remains active at the current observation.

12. **Boundary condition:** the active boundary condition, recorded as periodic or no-flux for the preregistered B1 conditions.

13. **Registered intervention status:** which, if any, preregistered intervention has occurred, including drive removal, local damage or boundary modification.

14. **Seed identity:** the explicit preregistered confirmatory simulation seed associated with the run.

The confirmatory analysis additionally derives condition-specific outcome variables from these measurements: terminal \(V\)-field standard deviation, time to heterogeneity collapse after drive removal, immediate central-region damage fraction, time to 90-percent central-region recovery, terminal recovery fraction, and terminal heterogeneity after boundary modification.

Variables used to identify technically invalid runs are also recorded through the provenance system, including manifest and configuration hashes, seed consistency, software/source version, numerical-finiteness checks and raw-data integrity checks. These variables are used only to determine execution validity and are not scientific exclusion criteria based on the observed hypothesis outcome.
registration_responses.344-66:
No composite scalar measure of organisation, viability or self-maintenance will be constructed. The registered quantities remain separate because they answer different descriptive or intervention-specific questions.

The principal derived variables are defined as follows.

**1. Whole-field spatial heterogeneity**

For a \(V\) field containing \(N\) lattice sites,

$$
s_V =
\sqrt{
\frac{1}{N}
\sum_{i=1}^{N}
(V_i-\bar V)^2
}.
$$

The terminal heterogeneity measure is \(s_V\) at PDE step 6000.

For the sustained-pattern condition, the primary group-level estimand is the arithmetic mean of terminal \(s_V\) across the ten preregistered seeds.

For the non-pattern comparator, the same terminal quantity is used, allowing the two regimes to be assessed using the same measurement definition.

**2. Time to collapse after drive removal**

Driving is removed at PDE step 3500. For each seed, collapse time is

$$
T_{\mathrm{collapse}}
=
\min \{t-3500 : s_V(t) \leq 0.005\}.
$$

If the threshold is not reached during the registered post-intervention observation window, the run is recorded as not meeting the registered collapse criterion.

The secondary drive-removal measure is terminal \(s_V\) at PDE step 6000.

**3. Immediate local-damage fraction**

Let \(C_{\mathrm{pre}}\) denote the central-region mean \(V\) value at the last registered observation before the local-damage intervention, and let \(C_{\mathrm{post}}\) denote the corresponding value immediately after the registered perturbation.

The immediate retained fraction is

$$
R_{\mathrm{immediate}}
=
\frac{C_{\mathrm{post}}}{C_{\mathrm{pre}}}.
$$

The proportional deficit is

$$
D_{\mathrm{immediate}}
=
1-R_{\mathrm{immediate}}.
$$

A reduction of at least 50 percent corresponds to \(R_{\mathrm{immediate}} \leq 0.5\).

**4. Local-damage recovery time**

Recovery time is the first registered post-damage time at which central-region mean \(V\) returns to at least 90 percent of its pre-damage value:

$$
T_{\mathrm{recovery}}
=
\min\{t-3500 :
C(t) \geq 0.9\,C_{\mathrm{pre}}\}.
$$

The terminal recovery fraction is

$$
R_{\mathrm{terminal}}
=
\frac{C(6000)}{C_{\mathrm{pre}}}.
$$

**5. Boundary-robustness measure**

For the boundary-modification condition, the principal derived measure is terminal whole-field \(V\) standard deviation at PDE step 6000 after the boundary is changed from periodic to no-flux at PDE step 3500.

**6. Adjacent-cell spatial mutual information**

The \(V\) field is discretised into 12 equally spaced bins spanning its observed minimum-to-maximum range. Mutual information for adjacent-cell pairs is calculated as

$$
I(X;Y)
=
\sum_{x,y}
p(x,y)
\log
\frac{p(x,y)}
{p(x)p(y)}.
$$

Horizontal and vertical adjacent-cell mutual information values are averaged. Under periodic boundaries, neighbouring cells wrap across the lattice edges; under non-periodic boundaries only existing adjacent pairs are included.

If whole-field \(s_V < 10^{-5}\), spatial mutual information is set to zero. This preregistered amplitude gate prevents numerical remnants of an effectively homogeneous field from being interpreted as meaningful spatial structure.

**7. Spectral peak fraction**

The \(V\) field is first mean-centred. A two-dimensional discrete Fourier transform is calculated and squared magnitudes provide Fourier power. The zero-frequency/DC component is removed.

The spectral peak fraction is

$$
S_{\mathrm{peak}}
=
\frac{
\max_{\mathbf{k}\neq 0} P(\mathbf{k})
}{
\sum_{\mathbf{k}\neq 0}P(\mathbf{k})
}.
$$

If whole-field \(s_V < 10^{-5}\), this descriptor is set to zero.

Spatial mutual information and spectral peak fraction are secondary descriptive pattern measures only. They are not interpreted as measures of self-maintenance, viability or a universal degree of organisation.

**8. Condition-level seed counts**

Several preregistered decision rules additionally use the number of seeds satisfying a fixed quantitative criterion, for example the number of seeds with terminal \(s_V \geq 0.04\), the number reaching \(s_V \leq 0.005\) within 500 PDE steps after drive removal, or the number recovering to at least 90 percent of the pre-damage central-region mean within 500 PDE steps.

These counts are used only according to the preregistered condition-specific decision rules. They are not combined into a general hierarchy or organisation index.
registration_responses.344-71:
The primary confirmatory analysis does not use ANOVA, regression, structural equation modelling or another fitted parametric model. The preregistered hypotheses are evaluated using fixed quantitative estimands and decision thresholds specified before confirmatory execution.

All analyses are performed first at the individual-seed level and then aggregated across the ten preregistered confirmatory seeds. The same seed identities are used across conditions where the initialisation structure is shared, allowing paired descriptive comparisons, but the primary decisions are determined by the preregistered condition-specific rules rather than by null-hypothesis significance tests.

The five primary analyses are:

C1: Sustained pattern regime.
The primary estimand is the mean terminal (V)-field standard deviation at PDE step 6000 across the ten registered seeds. The analysis also counts how many seeds have terminal (V)-field standard deviation of at least 0.04.

C2: Non-pattern comparator.
The primary estimand is the mean terminal (V)-field standard deviation at PDE step 6000. The analysis also counts how many seeds have terminal (V)-field standard deviation at or below 0.005.

C3: Dependence on sustained driving.
For each seed, the primary estimand is the number of PDE steps elapsed after removal of driving at step 3500 until whole-field (V)-field standard deviation first reaches or falls below 0.005. The analysis counts the number of seeds meeting this collapse threshold within 500 PDE steps. Mean terminal (V)-field standard deviation at PDE step 6000 is a secondary registered estimand.

C4: Local damage and recovery.
For each seed, the immediate proportional reduction in central-region mean (V) following local damage is calculated relative to the last registered pre-damage value. Recovery time is the number of PDE steps after damage until central-region mean (V) first reaches at least 90 percent of its pre-damage value. The analysis counts the number of seeds showing an immediate reduction of at least 50 percent and subsequent recovery within 500 PDE steps.

C5: Boundary robustness.
The primary estimand is terminal whole-field (V)-field standard deviation at PDE step 6000 after the registered change from periodic to no-flux boundaries at step 3500. The analysis counts the number of seeds with terminal standard deviation of at least 0.04.

The sustained non-pattern comparator functions as a negative control for persistent spatial heterogeneity. The sustained pattern condition functions as the reference condition for the intervention analyses. Drive removal, local damage and boundary modification are registered interventions whose effects are evaluated against the corresponding frozen pre-intervention trajectory and/or sustained-driving reference.

No statistical model will be substituted if a preregistered threshold is not met. Any additional fitted model or inferential test introduced after confirmatory outcomes are observed will be labelled exploratory and will not replace the registered primary decision rules.
registration_responses.344-77:
Primary inference is based on preregistered quantitative decision rules rather than (p)-values, confidence-level significance thresholds, Bayes factors or model-fit indices. No one-tailed or two-tailed null-hypothesis significance tests are used for the primary decisions.

The condition-specific criteria are:

C1: Sustained pattern regime

Retain: mean terminal (V)-field standard deviation (\geq 0.05), and at least 9 of 10 seeds have terminal standard deviation (\geq 0.04).
Restrict: mean terminal standard deviation (\geq 0.02), but the Retain criterion is not met.
Reject: mean terminal standard deviation (<0.02), or the regime cannot be distinguished reproducibly from the matched non-pattern comparator.

C2: Non-pattern comparator

Retain: mean terminal (V)-field standard deviation (\leq 0.005), and at least 9 of 10 seeds are (\leq 0.005).
Restrict: mean terminal standard deviation (>0.005) but (\leq0.02).
Reject: mean terminal standard deviation (>0.02).

C3: Dependence on sustained driving

Retain: at least 9 of 10 seeds reach (V)-field standard deviation (\leq0.005) within 500 PDE steps after drive removal, and mean terminal standard deviation is (\leq0.005).
Restrict: quantitative collapse occurs in at least 8 of 10 seeds but exceeds the 500-step window or leaves terminal residual structure above 0.005.
Reduce: equivalent persistent patterning continues after drive removal, reducing the explanatory role assigned to sustained driving for this regime.
Reject: fewer than 8 of 10 seeds show quantitative collapse after registered drive removal.

C4: Local damage and recovery

Retain: at least 8 of 10 seeds show an immediate central-region mean-(V) reduction of at least 50 percent and recover to at least 90 percent of the pre-damage value within 500 PDE steps.
Restrict: damage is quantitatively effective but recovery occurs in fewer than 8 of 10 seeds or requires more than 500 PDE steps.
Reject: the registered perturbation fails to produce a selective local deficit or no reproducible recovery occurs under sustained driving.

C5: Boundary robustness

Retain: at least 8 of 10 seeds have terminal (V)-field standard deviation (\geq0.04).
Restrict: non-trivial heterogeneity remains but fewer than 8 of 10 seeds meet the 0.04 threshold.
Reject: the registered boundary modification eliminates reproducible non-trivial spatial heterogeneity.

The overall B1 verdict is assigned only after all five registered conditions have valid provenance and analysis records:

Retain: C1, C2 and C3 each meet their Retain criteria. C4 and C5 are reported as robustness characterisation.
Restrict: the core pattern/non-pattern/drive-dependence result is otherwise retained but one or both robustness tests show material sensitivity, or one core condition reaches only its Restrict criterion.
Reduce: the matched comparator or drive-removal condition reproduces the decisive persistence result such that the nominated pattern regime or sustained driving adds no selective explanatory value.
Suspend: a decisive condition is invalid, provenance-incomplete, numerically unstable or otherwise uninterpretable under the frozen protocol.
Reject: the sustained pattern regime is not quantitatively distinguishable from the comparator or reproducible dependence upon sustained driving is not demonstrated.

No multiple-testing correction is applied because the five hypotheses are not being searched for significance across a family of interchangeable null-hypothesis tests. Each has a separate preregistered estimand and decision rule, and the overall B1 verdict is itself preregistered. Secondary analyses cannot substitute for a failed primary criterion.
registration_responses.344-81:
No statistical imputation of missing confirmatory data is planned.

The protocol is designed to generate a complete set of registered outputs for every valid simulation run. If required raw fields, primary measurements, registered observations or provenance records are missing because of a technical execution failure, that run will not be analysed as partially observed scientific evidence. It will be classified as INVALID_RUN, the failure will be preserved in the audit record, and the same preregistered seed may be rerun after the technical cause has been corrected.

Seeds will not be replaced with new seeds because data are missing or because a run produces an unfavourable scientific outcome.

If a required condition cannot be completed validly after documented technical correction attempts, the missing decisive evidence will not be imputed or ignored. The relevant hypothesis or overall B1 judgement will be eligible for SUSPEND because the preregistered evidence required for interpretation is incomplete.
registration_responses.344-83:
Several secondary analyses are preregistered for descriptive and robustness purposes.

Adjacent-cell spatial mutual information and spectral peak fraction will be reported as secondary descriptors of spatial pattern structure. Both are subject to the preregistered (V)-field amplitude gate of (10^{-5}). These measures are not interpreted as scalar measures of organisation, viability or self-maintenance.

Per-seed trajectories of whole-field (V)-field standard deviation will be plotted to show temporal behaviour rather than only terminal aggregates. The local-damage condition will additionally report central-region trajectories so the immediate deficit and recovery process are visible.

Paired descriptive comparisons across conditions may be reported because the same ten seed identities are used where initialisation structures are shared. These comparisons may include per-seed differences in terminal heterogeneity and intervention-response timing. They are secondary to the registered categorical decision rules.

Raw and processed results will also be inspected for numerical stability and consistency with the registered intervention timing. Such checks are quality-control procedures rather than alternative hypothesis tests.

Any additional analysis conceived after the confirmatory results have been observed, including new statistical models, alternative thresholds, alternative spatial descriptors or post hoc subgrouping, will be explicitly labelled exploratory. Exploratory analyses may motivate a future preregistration but will not replace, reinterpret or rescue a failed preregistered primary criterion.
registration_responses.344-86:
This preregistration forms the first confirmatory experimental study within the Theory of Everything Research Programme described in the published Programme Overview and Working Papers I--III.

B1 is intentionally narrow. It does not test self-maintenance directly and does not attempt to establish life, autonomy, organisational closure or any higher-order dependency in the programme. Its role is to provide a controlled physical baseline demonstrating whether sustained non-equilibrium driving can support reproducible spatial organisation in a Gray--Scott reaction--diffusion system, and to characterise how that organisation responds to removal of driving, local perturbation and a change of boundary condition.

This distinction is methodologically important because persistent organisation must not be conflated with internally generated maintenance. B1 therefore establishes, at most, the weaker relation:

$$
\text{sustained non-equilibrium driving}
\longrightarrow
\text{persistent organised pattern}.
$$

It does not establish:

$$
\text{persistent organised pattern}
\longrightarrow
\text{self-maintenance}.
$$

A separate subsequent B2 experiment is planned to test causal maintenance architectures more directly through comparisons among passive persistence, external maintenance, internal feed-forward maintenance and reciprocal internal maintenance, including targeted ablation and functional rescue. Results from B1 will not be used to assume the outcome of B2.

Three development-only pilot seeds were used before this preregistration to validate the implementation and measurement procedures. Those pilot runs revealed two measurement issues: normalised spatial-pattern measures could appear spuriously large when field amplitude was effectively zero, and whole-lattice averaging could dilute the effect of a local-damage intervention. The confirmatory protocol was therefore revised before registration to include a \(V\)-field amplitude gate of \(10^{-5}\) for the relevant descriptive pattern measures and a registered central-region measure for the damage-and-recovery condition.

The resulting version 1.1.0 confirmatory protocol is explicitly pilot-informed. The ten confirmatory seeds are separate from the three development seeds and had not been executed, inspected or analysed when this preregistration was prepared. The confirmatory manifests, environment configurations, intervention definitions, seed set, estimands, thresholds and decision rules were frozen before registration and are accompanied by SHA-256 integrity records.

The experiment is implemented within a reproducible infrastructure developed before B1. That infrastructure provides manifest validation, frozen configuration checking, seed registration, raw trajectory logging, provenance capture, automated analysis, figure and table generation, machine-readable decision records and integrity verification. A confirmatory execution gate prevents the registered ten-seed study from running until this preregistration has been made public.

Any departure from the preregistered protocol after confirmatory execution begins will be documented explicitly. Analyses developed after inspection of confirmatory outcomes will be labelled exploratory and will not replace the registered primary decision criteria.

The broader methodological principle is that the experimental programme is designed to remove unsupported structure rather than preserve a preferred hierarchy. A valid negative result, restriction or successful alternative explanation is therefore treated as scientifically informative rather than as a failure of the programme.
